brief: Yesterday's (Sep 23) risk-off move traces a chain: a hot September PMI, with input-cost inflation up the most since 2020, triggered it, alongside Brent breaking back above $100 ($103.59) on Iran's UN rhetoric, a weak 3.20bp-tailed 5Y auction, and the 5Y yield breaking 5%, implying the market had under-priced terminal Fed funds. JPMorgan's Market Intel desk reads the PMI as pointing to ~5% real GDP growth, arguing this should still buttress SPX earnings (tied to nominal, not real, GDP) despite the inflation, and that strong consumer/corporate balance sheets mean a material slowdown needs time or more hikes, though bond vol, not yield levels, is the bigger equity risk. Traders stay tactically cautious pending three US/Iran scenarios this week: a deal brings a US short-squeeze rally led by RTY with EU outperforming; no deal/no escalation keeps AI/Tech leading a narrowing market (NDX>EU>SPX, breadth thinning); no deal with escalation returns oil to $100 and 10Y above 5%, pressuring equities while Tech/US outperform the decline. Core call: long Tech (Mag7/Memory/Semis) vs short RTY, possibly run dollar- or market-neutral, plus a Brazil/LatAm long as an AI-fear hedge; US seen tactically outperforming DM on higher yields and a stronger dollar.
